In Japan, a type of rice called “Musenmai” (rice that does not need to be washed) is being sold. This rice does not need to be washed before cooking.

Ordinary rice is washed with water before cooking. Why does rice need to be washed? Because a layer of “bran” (nuka) adheres to the surface of the grains. This bran does not taste good, so people wash the rice before eating it to remove it. No-wash rice is rice from which the bran has been removed by machinery, so it does not need to be washed.

Compared with washing rice with water, using special machinery to remove the bran does not damage the flavorful components on the surface of the grains. For this reason, some people say that no-wash rice tastes better.

If you want to travel to Tochigi Prefecture, where should you go and what would be fun to do?

First, there are the hot springs. Tochigi Prefecture has two hot springs that have been famous since long ago: Nasu Onsen and Kinugawa Onsen. People who like hot springs may want to visit both in one day. However, they are far apart, so I think that would be difficult. Why not stay overnight at one of them?

Another wonderful place is Lake Chuzenji in autumn. The scenery there is beautiful. The leaves around the lake turn red and yellow, so you can enjoy magnificent autumn colors. When you glide across the lake by boat, the scenery comes into full view and it feels extremely pleasant.

There are also many kinds of delicious food. Strawberries are especially good. 「Tochiotome」is a slightly small variety of strawberry. Later, a large strawberry called「Skyberry」was developed. 「Skyberry」is used in sweets. You can buy or enjoy both「Tochiotome」and「Skyberry」in many places throughout Tochigi Prefecture.

However, I thought Japanese food consisted entirely of raw dishes such as sushi, sashimi, and salad, and I believed that eating such food would make my body cold. Therefore, I did not eat Japanese food even once.

But one day, my friend Shoko said, 「I just found a great Japanese restaurant. Let's go together!」. I did not really want to go, but Shoko wanted to go with me, so I decided to go. First, I ate sushi. From then on, I came to like Japanese food and also began cooking Japanese dishes myself.

One day, while I was eating alone at a restaurant, the person sitting next to me started talking to me. They asked, "Where do you buy your clothes?" so I told them about several stores I liked.

Why would that person ask a first-time acquaintance something like that? They said they had gained weight since starting medication for an illness. Apparently, their old clothes no longer fit, which had caused them a great deal of trouble. They said they had looked at me and thought that perhaps we were the same size.

I felt a little sad when I heard that. Did I really look that fat? But the person complimented me: "You have such good taste." They said that because I was wearing a very nice outfit, they wanted to know which store I had bought it from. I felt better.

I said, "You can also buy clothes on the Internet." When they asked, "How do you do that?" I explained it to them. Since I did not explain while looking at a computer or smartphone, I was a little worried about whether they had really understood.

default.q.speeddoc_n4-t20-q1.verdict:
✅ Correct answer: (c) まえに買ったかばんも4割引にしてもらえるからです。
The reason is that by buying the bag currently discounted by 80%, the speaker calculates that both the previously purchased bag and the new one effectively receive a 40% discount on average.
default.q.speeddoc_n4-t20-q1.explanation: The direct basis for answering the question is the quotation: 「そうすれば、まえに買ったかばんは4割引、これから買うかばんも4割引になると考えたからです。」 (I thought that if I did that, the bag I had bought earlier would be 40% off, and the bag I was about to buy would also be 40% off.) Grammatically, the sentence uses the conditional 「～ば」 together with the reason pattern 「～と考えたからです」. The pattern 「～からだ / からです」 follows the plain form to express the reason or motive behind buying the items. In terms of meaning, the author psychologically reassures themself by using the 80% discount (8割引) on the new bag to offset the original price of the old bag, effectively treating both bags as 40% off (4割引). Note the trap in choice (a): 「買ったあと」 (after buying it) shows that giving the bag to a friend was a decision made after the purchase, not the original purpose.
default.q.speeddoc_n4-t20-q1.why.0: ✗ (a) Giving it to a friend was only a decision made after the purchase; the author was not looking for a bag to give as a gift from the beginning.
default.q.speeddoc_n4-t20-q1.why.1: ✗ (b) The discount bag is merely the general discount context; the core reason the author buys another one is the thought that the old bag might also be discounted.
default.q.speeddoc_n4-t20-q1.why.2: ✓ (c) The author reasons that if they buy this additional bag, the bag previously bought at the original price can also be regarded as being 40% off.
default.q.speeddoc_n4-t20-q1.why.3: ✗ (d) The passage does not mention at all that the author likes the types of bags sold at this store.
default.q.speeddoc_n4-t26-q2.verdict:
✅ Correct answer: (a) 朝の練習のまえ
The passage specifies that the students ate boxed lunches in the morning before the practice session began.
default.q.speeddoc_n4-t26-q2.explanation: The key N4 patterns are 「N の まえに」(before...) and 「N の あと」(after...). A noun combines with the particle の to establish the order of events. Based on the quotation 「そして、授業のまえに、みんなで朝ごはんのおべんとうを食べました。」, the complete translation is: "Then, before class, we all ate breakfast bento together." Although the passage later describes feelings after practice, the context here is the first-year students’ morning routine. To distinguish the choices, underline the question word 「いつ」(when) and carefully compare the nouns combined with time-order expressions such as 「練習」 and 「授業」.

default.q.speeddoc_n4-t26-q2.why.1: ✗ (b) Incorrect because there is no eating or drinking during the practice session (朝の練習中).

default.q.speeddoc_n4-t41-q4.verdict:
✅ Correct answer: (a) まえは日本料理を食べてもおいしいと思わなかったですが、今は好きになりました。
At first, the character assumed that Japanese food was fishy and made the stomach feel cold, so they did not think it was tasty. After a friend invited them to try it, they realized it was delicious and came to like it.
default.q.speeddoc_n4-t41-q4.explanation: The key grammar pattern is 「V-る / V-ない + ようになる」, which expresses a change in habit, state, or ability over time (“come to...,” “begin to...”); it is combined with the concessive pattern 「V-て + も」 (“even if...” ). Choice (a) means: “In the past, even when I ate Japanese food, I did not think it was delicious, but now I have come to like Japanese food.” The evidence is the author’s account: 「生の魚はくさいと思っていましたが、そのすしはぜんぜんくさくなくておいしかったです。」 (“I used to think raw fish smelled bad, but that sushi did not smell at all and was delicious”) and the concluding sentence: 「わたしはそれから日本料理が好きになり、日本料理を作るようにもなりました。」 (“After that, I came to like Japanese food and also began cooking Japanese food.”) For reading-comprehension questions about a character’s change, compare the past and present carefully. At the beginning, the author had already cooked for herself (「中華料理を作ったりして食べていました」), so choices (c) and (d) can quickly be eliminated.
default.q.speeddoc_n4-t41-q4.why.0: ✓ (a) This choice is correct because the character once thought raw fish smelled unpleasant and Japanese food was not tasty, but after experiencing it firsthand, changed their mind and came to enjoy Japanese cuisine.
default.q.speeddoc_n4-t41-q4.why.1: ✗ (b) This choice is incorrect because it does not express the key change in attitude and feelings: moving from the prejudice that the food would be unappetizing to liking Japanese food.
default.q.speeddoc_n4-t41-q4.why.2: ✗ (c) This choice is incorrect because, when the character first came to Japan, they already knew how to cook, preparing Chinese dishes themselves; they did not lack cooking skills.
default.q.speeddoc_n4-t41-q4.why.3: ✗ (d) This choice is incorrect because the character has now also begun cooking Japanese dishes at home; they have not switched to eating only at restaurants.
